system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 14:16:09 UTC, Explorer set a UserAssist registry value whose ROT13-encoded name decodes to a path for powershell.exe. This is consistent with PowerShell having been launched, but does not establish what it did.
The UserAssist update is about 36 minutes later than the reported appearance around 13:40 UTC, so this record does not establish that it was the same PowerShell window.
At 13:40 UTC, the proxy recorded ivy.chen browsing login.salesforce.com, including a successful page request; these records do not show PowerShell activity.

At 13:26 UTC, the proxy recorded a successful CONNECT to desktop.dropbox.com with a DropboxUpdate user agent. Dropbox is not among the approved services listed in the environment context, but this record alone does not show Dropbox file sharing or malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records contain the UserAssist registry update but no PowerShell process-creation event or command line, so they do not identify the launch time, parent process, arguments, script, or actions.
The proxy record identifies Dropbox updater traffic, but does not reveal whether files were uploaded or downloaded.
The available excerpt cannot establish whether relevant events were missing from collection or simply absent.
claims_not_established: That the PowerShell window reported around 13:40 UTC corresponds to the PowerShell path recorded in UserAssist at 14:16 UTC.
That PowerShell ran a script, performed suspicious actions, or was launched by a malicious actor.
That the Dropbox connection involved file sharing, data transfer beyond the recorded tunnel bytes, or compromise.
That the observed activity was authorized or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve endpoint process-creation and PowerShell logging for WS-ICHEN-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including command lines, PowerShell script-block/module logs, and console or transcript records.
Check endpoint artifacts such as Prefetch and relevant execution history to corroborate the PowerShell launch time and identify associated files or scripts.
Determine whether Dropbox is installed or otherwise authorized on WS-ICHEN-01 and review associated proxy or endpoint records for actual file-transfer activity.
Correlate the reported observation with user interview details and any available screen or endpoint telemetry.
